z-m-18-01.title: If 2 equations dey, solution always one pair?
z-m-18-01.topic: Linear equation systems with no solution or endless solutions
z-m-18-01.goal: Confirm by checking solutions, judging information, and making examples yourself say when you join 2 linear equations with 2 unknowns, solution get 3 possibilities (one pair, no solution, or endless solutions), and explain which condition make each one happen.
z-m-18-01.material:
Soyoung talk say, "If 2 linear equations with unknowns x and y dey, always get exactly one pair (x, y) wey satisfy both equations together." Here x and y fit be any numbers, and all equations linear with integer coefficients. Soyoung wan test her idea with the equation system below. Read am like this: 'x plus 2y equal 6', '2x plus 4y equal 10'.
  ㉠ x + 2y = 6
  ㉡ 2x + 4y = 10
z-m-18-01.thinking.0: Find and correct line in solution where conclusion come without evidence
z-m-18-01.thinking.1: Judge what more info needed to decide number of solutions
z-m-18-01.thinking.2: Make different equations yourself wey satisfy conditions and check dem
z-m-18-01.prereq.0: Know solution of linear equation with two unknowns na pair (x,y)
z-m-18-01.prereq.1: Meaning of solution of simultaneous equations (pair satisfying both at once)
z-m-18-01.prereq.2: Experience seeing linear equation ax+by=c as line on coordinate plane (Grade 8; no need know connection to solution counts)
z-m-18-01.s.s1.prompt: In solution below, Soyoung write work for ㉠ and ㉡. Choose line where evidence for conclusion missing. Set first idea (Soyoung claim) aside and check each equation.
z-m-18-01.s.s1.hint.0: Put (0,0) into left side of ㉠, x+2y=6, and check whether result 6. [0 0]
z-m-18-01.s.s1.hint.1: Tink whether same 2x+4y in line 2 fit equal both 12 and 10 at same time. [2 2 4 12 10]
z-m-18-01.s.s1.line.0: Multiply both sides of ㉠ x+2y=6 by 2: 2x+4y=12.
z-m-18-01.s.s1.line.1: Compare with ㉡ 2x+4y=10: left sides same, right sides differ, 12 and 10.
z-m-18-01.s.s1.line.2: So x and y cancel, so x=0,y=0 be solution.
z-m-18-01.s.s1.line.3: So this equation system get one solution pair (0,0). [0 0]
z-m-18-01.s.s1.explain: Line 3 no follow. Line 2 show same 2x+4y must be both 12 and 10, so no x,y value fit satisfy. “x and y cancel” no mean dem equal 0. Put (0,0) in ㉠ and you get 0=6, false. Line 4 carry line 3 mistake. [0 0]
z-m-18-01.s.s2.prompt: Keep ㉠ same and change ㉡ to 2x+4y=c. (c fit any number; value unknown. Read: 2x plus 4y equal c.) With info now, wetin you fit say about solutions?
z-m-18-01.s.s2.hint.0: Write equation from multiplying ㉠ both sides by 2, then compare side by side with ㉡ form.
z-m-18-01.s.s2.hint.1: Put 12 and one number different from 12 for c, then test whether two equations become same condition.
z-m-18-01.s.s2.o.a: Whatever c be, solution always one pair.
z-m-18-01.s.s2.r.a: Dis answer carry first belief say two equations mean one pair. You no check left side 2x+4y na twice ㉠ left side. [2 4 2]
z-m-18-01.s.s2.o.b: Whatever c be, no x,y satisfy both equations.
z-m-18-01.s.s2.r.b: You declare “dem no fit meet” by only looking at ㉡ left side. You no consider c fit make both equations same.
z-m-18-01.s.s2.o.c: We need c value. Depending on c, either no solution or infinitely many.
z-m-18-01.s.s2.o.d: If c=12, no solution; any other c give infinitely many.
z-m-18-01.s.s2.r.d: You find two cases but swap them. Check whether ㉡ become same as ㉠ when 2x+4y=12, twice 6. [2 4 12 2 6]
z-m-18-01.s.s2.explain: ㉡ left side 2x+4y na twice ㉠ left side. If c=12, both sides ㉠ double, so same condition and infinite solutions. If c≠12, same 2x+4y would need be another value than 12, so no solution. No c value give exactly one pair for this system. Need know c to say number of solutions. [2 4 2 12 12 2 4 12 2 6]
z-m-18-01.s.s3.prompt: Now make system with ㉠ x+2y=6 wey get no solution. Write new equation ax+by=c and make 2 different ones. (a,b,c integers; a,b not 0 and absolute value at most 20; c absolute value at most 100. Read ax+by=c as “a x plus b y equal c.”) [2 6 0 20 100]
z-m-18-01.s.s3.hint.0: Remember what happen in s2 when c no be 12, and compare relation between x/y coefficients and ㉠.
z-m-18-01.s.s3.hint.1: Choose a and b first, then change c and test whether any (x,y) satisfy both equations. Leave out c wey make same equation as ㉠.
z-m-18-01.s.s3.fail.c2: a,b no be 0, absolute value at most 20; c absolute value at most 100.
z-m-18-01.s.s3.ok.c3: Coefficients of x and y have same ratio as ㉠ (y coefficient twice x coefficient). [2]
z-m-18-01.s.s3.fail.c3: Check whether x/y coefficients keep same relation as ㉠. With dis form, lines meet at one point.
z-m-18-01.s.s3.ok.c4: Right-side constant no be same multiple as ㉠ (so e no be same equation).
z-m-18-01.s.s3.fail.c4: Dis equation same as ㉠, so infinite solutions. For no solution, right-side constant must differ.
z-m-18-01.s.s3.explain: With (a,b,c)=(1,2,5), x+2y must be both 6 and 5, so no solution. (2,4,7) and (−3,−6,−4) same type. (2,4,12) na twice ㉠, so same equation; (1,3,4) different coefficient relation, so lines meet once. Equations for same line, like (2,4,7) and (4,8,14), count as one. [1 2 5 2 6 5 2 4 7 3 6 4 2 4 12 2 1 3 4 2 4 7 4 8 14]
z-m-18-01.s.s4.prompt: Answer Soyoung: when statement “two equations always get exactly one solution pair” right and when wrong? Write cases for one, none, or infinitely many solutions, connect to coefficients and right-side constants.
z-m-18-01.s.s4.hint.0: Pair equations you make in s2 and s3 with ㉠ one by one, compare how many times its coefficients and right constant are.
z-m-18-01.s.s4.hint.1: Split into pairs with no solution, infinite solutions, and one solution pair; write what different in each.

z-m-18-01.s.s4.model.0: Soyoung statement no always correct. If x/y coefficient ratios differ, one solution pair. If coefficient ratio same but constant ratio differ, no solution. If constant ratio same too, same equation, so infinitely many solutions. For example x+2y=6 and 2x+4y=10 get no solution.
z-m-18-01.s.s4.model.1: Think of dem as two lines. Different slopes meet once, so one pair. Same slope but different position mean parallel, no meeting and no solution. If lines overlap, infinitely many. So two equations no always mean one pair.
z-m-18-01.s.s4.modelNote.1: Answer from graph view. Instead of coefficients and constants, e use slope and where line pass to say same thing.
